children: rose 0.51% premarket after the FAA approved a waiver of airplane emissions rules allowing it to sell another 35 777F freighters for three years beyond January 2028, when new rules would have barred them. Boeing requested the approval in December 2025, citing customer demand and a delay in certifying the replacement aircraft.

The 777F is the only large widebody freighter in production, and its successor the 777-8F is not expected in service until roughly 2029. Boeing has said it expects to deliver the first 777-8F about two years after the first 777-9, currently targeted for 2027. The FAA said the waiver gives flexibility and accommodates uncertainty in the certification timeline.

Boeing says each 777F exported to a foreign customer contributes $440 million to the US trade balance at list price, and that more than $15 billion of exports could have been lost without the exemption. The FAA estimates the 35 aircraft would raise freighter operations by around 2% and fuel burn by around 8% against 2024 global freighter operations. Congress passed similar relief for the 767 freighter in 2024, running through 2033.

title: FAA Authorizes Boeing to Sell More 777Fs
